claims.summary: Over a field, on the cube {0,1}^n with C_D the degree-D part of the Boolean ideal, for a hypergraph H of nonempty blocks B with families (x_i)_{i in B}, approximators P_B in F[x_B] of degree <=a and K+a+1<=D: if each P_B is nonzero at some nonzero pattern of B, every common multiplier f (f P_B x_i in C_D) nonzero on the cube has degree >= tau(H), the transversal number; over F_p Pang's factors on a chain, prod_j(1-(x_{b_j}-x_{b_{j+1}})^(p-1)), nonzero exactly at 0 and 1_B, attain it with prod_{i in T}(1-x_i), T a least transversal, when tau(H)+a+1<=D. Over F_2 every product of s<=|B|-1 of Pang's factors meets the hypothesis, and s>=|B| factors allow f=1. Over F_2 on all (t+1)-subsets with t factors the least degree is n-t (attained when D>=n+1), the baseline prod(1+x_i) of degree n survives every choice, and for pairs (n>=4) a cyclic choice forces degree n; Pang's criterion S(1-eta)^t<1 with these t factors fails as an inequality at every 1<=K<=n when C(n,t+1)>=2^t, in particular for n>=2t+1.
claims.assessment: Working proof passed by the sole fresh-context medium reviewer with a follow-up (review record in research/results/common_multiplier_block_families_20261016); part (e) is the reviewer's construction, checked; the cube domain model only.
claims.rationale: Calibrates Pang's summed criterion with t=|B|-1 factors on an unbounded family: the criterion certifies nothing where prod(1+x_i) survives at degree n and the chain at n-t; the saving is a union of supports in a domain model, which the joint-savings endpoint excludes.
claims.next_action: Test the same families in the functional pigeonhole closure, where the chain errors are degree-2 monomials.
